title: 2026 Bespoked Osaka Picks 02: Alps, BTCHN, Cherubim, Curve, Yanagi – John Watson
content:
Maido from Osaka! Cari and John were in attendance at the 2026 Bespoked Osaka event, where they documented a variety of bikes from the global framebuilding community. Read on for a look at the Bespoked Osaka venue and a selection of builders including Alps, BTCHN, Cherubim, Curve, and Yanagi…

Alps Climber Ti

Hiroshi Hagiwara founded the Japanese brand Sports Cycle Alps, and it closed 19 years ago. Hitoshi Omae recently relaunched the brand and to commemorate the relaunch, Hitoshi pinged Japanese framebuilder Moriai to build a titanium frameset, designed to mimic the lines of a traditional steel bike.

Mated with a steel fork, which Atelier Kinopio painted closely to match the color of the frame, the Alps Climber Ti planes and flexes while weighing a scant 8.7kg, including the Kimura Manufacturing Co flashlight.

The bike features special chainrings, designed for the TA cranks and 10-speed chains, and features a 25-tooth inner ring, which, if you are a fan of TA cranks, you’ll know usually only go to 26 teeth. If you’re interested in buying a complete bike as shown, it’ll set ya back a cool 1,100,000 yen, or around $ 7,000 USD.

@VeloApres

BTCHN 32er Lefty

Tyler Reiswig, owner and builder at Chico, California’s BTCHN Bikes, rarely leaves his home in Butte County. This trip was his first time traveling internationally. When Silca offered to take him to Japan for Bespoked, he built up a wild 32er hardtail, paired with a Lefty fork and some handlebars that sparked lively conversations all weekend at the 2026 Bespoked Osaka show.

While they look obtuse with four brake levers, there is some methodology to the madness, Tyler explained. Typically, when you’re in aero bars, you lack brake levers, so Tyler mated the brake lines for the XT and GRX brakes and added blips to shift the derailleur, on top of a normal AXS shifter.

His decision to choose a Lefty fork came from a quest for stiffness. Other forks he’d used were too noodly and twisted unreasonably. The lefty was not only the stiffest option out there, but also the lightest. Tyler machined a volume spacer to adapt it to the 32er wheelsize and Berd built him custom wheels for the Lefty hub.

Combing through the bike’s details in and out of post typhoon light rain showers, piercing, warm sunlight, and deep, cold clouds, the light and color temperature shifted throughout our 30-minute conversation and photo shoot. Spending extra time with all of Tyler’s show bikes unfurls the builder’s intent with his brand. Making custom, one-off bikes is time-intensive, and being a one-person shop doesn’t afford him the ability to open a build queue these days. So he spends extra time with these show bikes, used to showcase his creative thinking and practical execution of a bricolage of machined and 3D sintered components.

Tyler, it was good to see you out of your comfort zone, outside of your hometown, and experimenting with creative solutions for common problems. Who knows if the bars will be available and when, but the fact that they exist is extra special. Enjoy Japan homie!

@BTCHNBikes

Cherubim NJS Keirin Racer

Japanese craftsmanship, design, and tradition, all rolled into one bike. Cherubim’s Shinichi Konno built this bike in 2016 for Yuichiro Kamiyama, the highest earning Keirin racer in Japanese history. Keirin, for the uninitiated, is a form of motor-paced track bicycle racing originating in Japan in 1948.

Keirin racing follows Japan’s JKA racing format, in which tactical team formations cooperate before breaking away for the final sprint. Components used in Keirin require NJS certification and can be denoted by a special NJS stamp in place. Builders also must follow this certification, and it is an honor to achieve the label. Keirin is also a legal, government-regulated public gambling sport. Racers can earn a healthy living, with riders like Yuichiro Kamiyama raking in over 229,907,532 yen over his career.

As Yuichiro Kamiyama’s racing pedigree has earned him a lot of yen, Konno-san mixed gold flake glitter into the clear coat of the frame. Paired with Cherubim’s meticulously crafted lugwork and NJS-certified construction, this bike embodies Japanese construction and heritage.

I was lucky enough to have Konno-san magically appear outside while shooting his bike for a portrait.

@Cherubim

Curve Big Kev 32er Prototype 1

This was the first Big Kev that Melbourne, Australia-based Curve Cycling built to test out the emerging 32er wheelset. First debuted at the Spoken event in Australia, the bike has since undergone a stunning turquoise paint job, laid down by Candy Factory Paintworks, operated by co-founder Steve Varga. The second prototype was displayed at the 2026 Bespoked Dresden show.

Built around a 2.4″ tire with clearance for more, the Big Kev 32er features a Mone trip-plane fork and is built from a mixture of Columbus tubing. A special chainstay yoke ensures tire, chainring, and q-factor alignment without the need for obtuse crimping and the chopped seat stay ends terminate at the top tube in a bed of brass.

Once again, Curve displays its abilities, and Jimmy brings the heat!

@CurveCycling

Yanagi Kazusa Adventure Gravel Bike

Kamagaya City, Japan-based Yanagi brought one of its Kazusa adventure gravel bikes to the 2026 Bespoked Osaka showcase. This bike is the result of extensive collaboration between builder Koichi Iizumi and Sukiyaki Bikes, who did the custom pantography on the White Industries cranks. Then, as the final touch, Rintaro Shimoyama from Ghooost did the hand lettering over the plating, which was done by Nitto.

The talent of Sukiyaki is on full display here, with elaborate panto carvings in the White cranks, which took the artist two months to complete. The other parts on the bike – the stem spacer, headset cap, and head badge took another few months to complete.

Upon completion, this bike embodies what is so wonderful about the small maker community, particularly in Japan. Three talented makers coming together, working on a bike – which was plated by the legends at Nitto – all for a special show like Bespoked Osaka.

There was a great reverence felt with these talented humans. Myself for their craft and them for my hard work documenting it. Moments like this bring an intense sense of honor and pride for what we do over here at The Radavist: two decades of love and reverence for the global maker community.

Sugoi! Yanagi, Sukiyaki, Rintaro.

@Yanagi @Sukiyaki @Ghooost
